topic: Sleep is built, not owed (single): morning grogginess
caption:
Feeling heavy in the morning is not always proof you needed more sleep.

The brain does not wake all at once. That slow, foggy feeling is called sleep inertia, and it is usually strongest in the first half hour, then eases. After a poor night it can feel like a reason to go back to bed, when often it is the brain coming online.

From our blog on sleep drive. Full article: link in bio.

Research:
